Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished, high-fidelity visual direction board for Farbtupf, a tablet learning and drawing app for first graders in Zürich. The user is choosing a coherent design for the entire app because the current graphics feel cheap and inconsistent. The design must feel commissioned, original, thoughtful and child-friendly.
COMPOSITION: a crisp high-resolution landscape 3:2 board on a quiet neutral background. At the top, the direction number and name in handsome presentation typography. Show three clearly separated front-on app screenshots: a large landscape home screen taking the left 58% of the board, and two smaller landscape activity screens stacked on the right. No physical devices, hands, photography, skewed screens or decorative desk props. Every screen should look like the same shippable app. Along the bottom, show a small coordinated art sampler: an original fox portrait, a Zürich tram by a lakeside tree, a colouring-page outline of the same fox, four tool icons and five palette swatches. Use the same fox anatomy, medium, line treatment, icon rules, palette and typography across ALL screens and sampler.
HOME: app name "Farbtupf", a welcoming original fox character integrated into a simple scene, clear child-sized navigation, and six touch cards with exact labels "Zahlen", "Wörter", "Natur", "Formen", "Malen", "Meine Bilder". Cards have distinctive custom illustrations, not emoji. A tiny settings icon and understated progress indicator.
TOP RIGHT: learning screen titled "Sternenrakete", text "Wie viele fehlen?", an illustrated rocket beside five fuel/star places with exactly three filled and two empty, and large answer buttons "1", "2", "3". Keep the exercise visually obvious and uncluttered.
BOTTOM RIGHT: art screen titled "Malatelier", an unfinished original colouring illustration of the fox in a park: half coloured, half clean outline, with a large white working area, restrained custom tool icons and a simple coordinated colour palette. Include labels "Zurück" and "Speichern". It is a working drawing interface, not a generic cartoon picture.
TYPE & USABILITY: large clear early-reader sans-serif labels with strong contrast; decorative character only in the brand wordmark. Unambiguous silhouette icons; large touch targets; deliberate white space; consistent corner radii and alignment. All German labels accurately spelled. This is a design proposal, not an official teaching-material brand. Do not add publisher logos, standard system emoji, stock clipart, generic glossy gradients, thick black sticker outlines, hard black offset shadows, badges everywhere, tiny UI copy or random extra text.

directions.name: Waldatelier
directions.summary: Watercolour storybook · moss, cream and terracotta
directions.brief:
Direction title exactly "01 · Waldatelier".
ART DIRECTION: a refined contemporary watercolour-and-gouache children's picture book. Softly painted orange fox with expressive eyes, mossy woodland, warm ivory paper, muted sky blue, marigold and terracotta. Subtle pigment granulation only inside illustration; UI surfaces remain clear and smooth. Warm, calm, welcoming, beautifully observed original woodland art. No fluffy kawaii shorthand. Small botanical details, airy compositions, confident silhouettes.
UI: creamy canvas, deep forest-green typography, gentle pill buttons, a large scenic welcome panel and spacious cream cards with small painted vignettes. Thin sepia icons drawn from the same visual vocabulary. Very subtle shadows. Characterful title, practical Andika-like body type. Paint screen art retains the same fox proportions and uses clean sepia outlines which can be filled. The rocket is a charming painted wooden toy, not shiny 3D. Cohesion comes from restrained natural colour, painterly artwork and clean, quiet controls.

directions.name: Formenfreude
directions.summary: Swiss graphic design · precise shapes, vivid colour
directions.brief:
Direction title exactly "02 · Formenfreude".
ART DIRECTION: joyful Swiss modernist graphic design for children. Original flat geometric vector illustrations built from circles, arcs, triangles and honest colour blocks. Cream background, saturated ultramarine, coral red, warm sunflower yellow, a little turquoise, charcoal type. The orange fox is made from carefully balanced geometric shapes, recognisable rather than abstract to a child. Tram, rocket, icons, landscape and fox all share the same exact geometric construction. No gradients or paper texture, no generic stock icon pack.
UI: precise modular grid, bold large readable sans-serif typography, generous margins, simple flat rounded rectangles, colour used as functional grouping, restrained 12px corner-radius feeling, crisp alignments. Strong but sophisticated playfulness, editorial clarity. Use a lively asymmetrical bento layout for the home without sacrificing six clear labelled choices. Toolkit icons use uniform simple 2px-ish strokes. Drawing screen's uncoloured fox uses exactly the same geometric silhouette. Everything feels designed as a system, not an assortment of colourful cartoons.

directions.name: Papierwelt
directions.summary: Layered cut paper · tactile, handmade and warm
directions.brief:
Direction title exactly "03 · Papierwelt".
ART DIRECTION: exquisite layered cut-paper collage, like a carefully handmade illustrated children's art book. Original fox, tram, trees, rocket and small objects made from purposeful cut coloured paper shapes with subtly irregular edges, a hint of fibre, shallow consistent cast shadows between layers. Palette of warm oat, sage, dusty cornflower blue, burnt orange, peach and deep indigo. Premium craftsmanship, readable shapes, no messy scrapbooking or photoreal classroom objects.
UI: a quiet cream paper base, softly rounded paper panels, integrated paper chapter tabs, clear dark sans-serif labels; small tactility confined to illustration and restrained layering. Home looks like opening a well-organised illustrated activity book, with six clean paper cards and a larger little woodland collage. Drawing tools follow one simple cut-paper silhouette system. For the colouring area, show clean original outline art derived from the exact collage fox shapes, with a partly filled collage-colour treatment. Do not draw literal scissors, glue, tape corners, torn notebook clutter or buttons at random angles. This is a tidy usable digital app with a tactile art language, not a photograph of a craft table.

directions.name: Kleine Welten
directions.summary: Matte clay miniatures · soft, sculptural and playful
directions.brief:
Direction title exactly "04 · Kleine Welten".
ART DIRECTION: custom art-directed matte clay miniatures with gentle studio lighting. Original little fox sculpture, sculpted trees, toy Zürich tram and rocket; all have the same softly modelled clay material, subtle handmade imperfections and proportions. Warm ivory UI, periwinkle, apricot, muted mint and soft coral, deep ink typography. The artwork feels like high-end stop-motion set design, not glossy game assets. The fox is curious and appealing with a distinct long tail and small triangular ears, not an off-the-shelf mascot.
UI: keep controls flat and legible, with softly rounded cream cards, generous breathing room and minimal elevation; put the 3D material in the artwork rather than making every control a bulky toy. Home has a captivating small scene and six equally clear touch tiles featuring coordinated miniatures. The rocket activity is a matte sculpted toy with simple matching star counters. Art screen uses a clean line drawing of the same fox form, partly filled with the same palette, because the working canvas must remain easy to draw on. Tool icons are simplified consistent rounded silhouettes. Avoid photoreal devices, faux glass, metallic shine, plastic gloss, neon, confetti and thick cartoon outlines.

directions.name: Tintenabenteuer
directions.summary: Illustrated ink · expressive linework and storybook charm
directions.brief:
Direction title exactly "05 · Tintenabenteuer".
ART DIRECTION: an elegant contemporary illustrated adventure journal for young children. Beautiful original hand-inked linework with subtle variation, selective flat gouache colour fills, whimsical fox with a distinctive angular snout and flowing tail; understated little narrative scenes. Warm ivory, midnight navy, vermilion, muted teal and golden ochre. Linework is delicate but confident and readable; characters look commissioned for an illustrated book, not simplistic doodles. Use the same navy line weight hierarchy for fox, tram, rocket, tools, nature and colouring pages.
UI: quiet editorial storybook layout, ivory background, generous margins, large readable sans-serif activity labels, warm hand-lettered wordmark only. Home uses a wide illustrated welcome vignette and a clear two-column chapter-card grid with navy rules and small consistent ink illustrations. Avoid loud comic-book bursts and playful text distortion. Draw the rocket and counters with the same ink language. Drawing screen naturally shows half of the fox artwork coloured, with an uncluttered navy-outline tool strip. Art sampler demonstrates beautiful finished illustration and clean accessible colouring outlines as parts of the same system.
